description:
Found while building fz-4t3.1. native_codegen/function.rs (about line 155) passes a hardcoded None as block_env into lower_prim, and the parameter is threaded through about 15 functions in prim.rs, type_pred.rs, value.rs and support.rs. No caller passes Some, so every read of it is dead.

Removed:
- The block_env parameter from lower_prim and every function it is threaded through, with the dead Some arms that read it.
- The two #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] attributes in prim.rs (emit_variadic_extern_call, lower_prim): clippy.toml sets the threshold to 16, so they suppress nothing.

Done when: grep -rn block_env src/compiler2/native_codegen is empty, and grep -rn too_many_arguments src/compiler2/native_codegen is empty.

Acceptance: full gate green; no pin, golden or expected-output file changes; generated code identical over the 42-fixture sample (probe.sh from fz-4t3.1).
title: The always-None block_env parameter leaves lower_prim
